newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, February 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, February 27.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- The Revenue Commissioners have suspended the seeking of VAT payments from private crches pending a decision on whether commercial child-care services are partly exempt from the tax.
- The EU Livestock Exporters Association of Ireland has accused the Minister for Agriculture Ivan Yates of being anti-live exports and of not helping them to get animals out of the state.
- Unionists are expected to argue strenuously for the continuation of the Northern Ireland Forum during the British general election campaign.
- Cambridge Mineral Resources, a British exploration company has found a small quantity of sapphires in Donegal, Ireland.

- Alan Greenspan, the chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve, on Wednesday sent another strong signal to financial markets that the U.S. Central Bank was increasingly concerned about the impact on the economy of the continuing surge in equity prices. IRISH INDEPENDENT
- Emergency short-term plans to tackle overcrowding in Ireland's 14 jails have been authorised by Justice Minister Nora Owen.
- Ireland's business tycoon Ben Dunne has handed over a second document to Judge Gerard Buchanan in a dramatic development in the "payments to politicians" controversy.

- Ireland's Deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring on Wednesday night said Ulster Unionist leader David Trimble should be looking for consultation rather than saying there was going to be a repeat of Drumcree this year.
- American share prices fell on Wednesday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan rattled Wall Street by questioning the sustainability of the market's powerful rally.
- Irish Life's status as the latest billion pound company on the Dublin market was maintained on Wednesday when the shares rose another three pence to 329 pence.
- The Irish government on Wednesday night tried to distance itself from the potentially damaging pre-election decision to impose 21 percent VAT on child-minding.
- The Irish government is expected to move quickly to close off tax loopholes after a surprise court decision that the wife of John Gilligan was not liable for a tax bill of 1.6 million Irish pounds.
- Sexual harassment, domestic violence and pornography are among the vital issues that will be tackled by the Women's Rights Committee this year, the organisation said on Wednesday night.
- The early years of Economic Monetary Union could be quite difficult, according to a leading Irish economist.
- Irish inflation is defying conventional wisdom by falling despite a booming economy.
